correctness.rationale: The pair-majority construction is proved directly by the two-of-three intersection argument and exact counting. For n=3 through 10, the compatibility-graph equivalence was reconstructed and a complete Bron--Kerbosch enumeration was executed; every enumerated maximum clique exactly matched the generated classification, including all edge cases and codegree-three pairs.

originality.rationale: The 2026 source states the conjectured bound, fixed-progression sharp example, and a weaker general density theorem, but not these exact small-order classifications or the pair-majority equality construction. Targeted exact-claim, synonym, parameter, and stronger-coverage searches found no matching published result; this remains a best-of-knowledge assessment.

value.rationale: The result verifies the open conjectured optimum through order ten and exhibits a nonprincipal sharp construction valid for every n at least 7, showing that any future equality classification must allow more than fixed-progression stars.
